questions.q: A force $\overrightarrow{\mathrm{F}}=2 \hat{i}+\mathrm{b} \hat{j}+\hat{k}$ is applied on a particle and it undergoes a displacement $\hat{i}-2 \hat{j}-\hat{k}$. What will be the value of $b$, if work done on the particle is zero.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & w=0 \\ & \therefore \quad \vec{F} \cdot S=0 \\ & (2 \hat{i}+b \hat{j}+\hat{k}) \cdot(\hat{i}-2 \hat{j}-\hat{k})=0 \\ & 2-2 b-1=0 \\ & b=\frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}$

questions.q: A boy is rolling a <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>0</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>5</mn><mo> </mo><mi>kg</mi></math> ball on the frictionless floor with the speed of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>20</mn><msup><mrow><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi></mrow><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mo>.</mo></math> The ball gets deflected by an obstacle on the way. After deflection it moves with <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>5</mn><mo>%</mo></math> of its initial kinetic energy. What is the speed of the ball now?
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Given, m=0.5 kg and u=20 m s-1

Initial kinetic energy ki=12mu2

=12×0.5×20×20=100 J

After deflection it moves with 5% of ki

∴kf=5100×ki⇒5100×100

⇒kf=5 J

Now, let the final speed be 'v'  m s-1, then:

kf=5=12mv2

⇒v2=20

⇒v=20=4.47 m s-1

questions.q:
A body of $m \mathrm{~kg}$ slides from rest along the curve of vertical circle from point $A$ to $B$ in friction less path. The velocity of the body at $B$ is:
$\text { (given, } R=14 \mathrm{~m}, g=10 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}^2 \text { and } \sqrt{2}=1.4 \text { ) }$
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution: Apply W.E.T. from A to B $\begin{aligned} & \Rightarrow \mathrm{W}_{\mathrm{mg}}=\mathrm{K}_{\mathrm{B}}-\mathrm{K}_{\mathrm{A}} \\ & \Rightarrow \mathrm{mg} \times\left(\frac{\mathrm{R}}{\sqrt{2}}+\mathrm{R}\right)=\frac{1}{2} \mathrm{mv}_{\mathrm{B}}^2-0\left\{\mathrm{v}_{\mathrm{A}}=0 \text { rest }\right\} \\ & \Rightarrow \mathrm{mgR} \frac{(\sqrt{2}+1)}{\sqrt{2}}=\frac{1}{2} \mathrm{mv}_{\mathrm{B}}^2 \\ & \Rightarrow \sqrt{\mathrm{gR} \frac{2(\sqrt{2}+1)}{\sqrt{2}}}=\mathrm{v}_{\mathrm{B}} \\ & \Rightarrow \sqrt{\frac{10 \times 14 \times 2(2.4)}{1.4}}=\mathrm{v}_{\mathrm{B}} \\ & \Rightarrow 21.9=\mathrm{v}_{\mathrm{B}} \end{aligned}$

questions.q: The ratio of powers of two motors is $\dfrac{3\sqrt{x}}{\sqrt{x}+1}$, that are capable of raising 300 kg water in 5 minutes and 50 kg water in 2 minutes respectively from a well of 100 m deep. The value of $x$ will be
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Power of a motor is given by $P = \dfrac{mgh}{t}$.

For the first motor, the power is $P_1 = \dfrac{300 \times g \times 100}{5 \times 60}$.

For the second motor, the power is $P_2 = \dfrac{50 \times g \times 100}{2 \times 60}$.

The ratio of their powers is $\dfrac{P_1}{P_2} = \dfrac{\dfrac{300}{5}}{\dfrac{50}{2}} = \dfrac{60}{25} = \dfrac{12}{5}$.

Equating this to the given expression:

$\dfrac{3\sqrt{x}}{\sqrt{x} + 1} = \dfrac{12}{5}$

$\dfrac{\sqrt{x}}{\sqrt{x} + 1} = \dfrac{4}{5}$

$5\sqrt{x} = 4\sqrt{x} + 4$

$\sqrt{x} = 4 \Rightarrow x = 16$

questions.q: A body of mass <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>0</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>5</mn><mo> </mo><mi>kg</mi></math> travels on straight line path with velocity <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>v</mi><mo>=</mo><mfenced><mrow><mn>3</mn><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow></mfenced><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math>. The net work done by the force during its displacement from <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></math> to <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></math> is
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Given: v=3x2+4

Initial and final velocities are vi=302+4=4 m s-1

and vf=322+4=16 m s-1

From work-energy theorem,

⇒ΔKE=12mvf2-vi2

⇒ΔKE=12×12162-42

⇒ΔKE=W=60 J

questions.q: A wedge of mass <math><mi>M</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn><mi>m</mi></math> lies on a frictionless plane. A particle of mass <math><mi>m</mi></math> approaches the wedge with speed <math><mi>v</mi><mo>.</mo></math> There is no friction between the particle and the plane or between the particle and the wedge. The maximum height climbed by the particle on the wedge is given by:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
From conservation of linear momentum,

mv=4m+mvf
vf=v5
From conservation of mechanical energy,
12mv2=124m+mvf2+mgh
v2=5vf2+2gh
v2=5×v52+2gh
h=2v25g

questions.q: A body of mass <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>2</mn><mo> </mo><mi>kg</mi></math> begins to move under the action of a time dependent force given by <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mover><mi>F</mi><mo>→</mo></mover><mo>=</mo><mfenced><mrow><mn>6</mn><mi>t</mi><mo> </mo><mover><mi mathvariant="normal">i</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mo>+</mo><mn>6</mn><msup><mi>t</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo> </mo><mover><mi mathvariant="normal">j</mi><mo>^</mo></mover></mrow></mfenced><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">N</mi></math>. The power developed by the force at the time <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>t</mi></math> is given by:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Given: F→=6t i^+6t2 j^ N

Now, F→=ma→=6t i^+6t2 j^

⇒a→=F→m=3t i^+3t2 j^

Hence, velocity v→=∫0ta→dt=3t22i^+t3j^

Required power, P=F→.v→=9t3+6t5 W

questions.q: A stone of mass <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>m</mi></math>, tied to a string is being whirled in a vertical circle with a uniform speed. The tension in the string is
options: minimum when the rope is in the horizontal position.
minimum at the highest position of the circular path.
minimum at the lowest position of the circular path.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
As the speed is constant, centripetal force required towards the centre of the circle will be same. At the top, direction of gravitational force and tension acting on the object will be same. Therefore, we can write,

mg+T=mv2r ⇒T=mv2r-mg.

 Clearly in this case, tension in the string will be minimum.

questions.q: A particle of charge <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>q</mi></math> and mass <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>m</mi></math> is subjected to an electric field <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>E</mi><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>E</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mfenced><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>–</mo><mi>a</mi><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></mfenced></math> in the <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>x</mi><mo>-</mo></math>direction, where a and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>E</mi><mn>0</mn></msub></math> are constants. Initially the particle was at rest at <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></math>. Other than the initial position the kinetic energy of the particle becomes zero when the distance of the particle from the origin is :
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Wex=ΔK       K1-K1=0

∫0xqEdx=0

 q ∫0xE01-Qx2dx=0

qE0∫0x1-ax2dx=0

x-ax33=0

1-ax23=0

ax23=1

x2=3a

x=3a

questions.q:
Identify the correct statements from the following:

(A) Work done by a man in lifting a bucket out of a well by means of a rope tied to the bucket is negative

(B) Work done by gravitational force in lifting a bucket out of a well by a rope tied to the bucket is negative

(C) Work done by friction on a body sliding down an inclined plane is positive

(D) Work done by an applied force on a body moving on a rough horizontal plane with uniform velocity is zero

(E) Work done by the air resistance on an oscillating pendulum is negative

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Work done is given by, W=Fscosθ, where θ is the angle between the force and the displacement.

case(A): Direction of force and displacement both are in the same direction and hence work done will be positive. Hence, wrong.

case(B): Direction of force and displacement both are in the opposite direction and hence work done will be negative. Hence, correct.

case(C): Direction of force and displacement both are in the opposite direction and hence work done will be negative. Hence, wrong.

case(D): Direction of force and displacement both are in the same direction and hence work done will be positive. Hence, wrong.

case(E): Direction of force and displacement both are in the opposite direction and hence work done will be negative. Hence, correct.

questions.q: A bob of mass $m$ is suspended at a point $O$ by a light string of length $l$ and left to perform vertical motion (circular) as shown in figure. Initially, by applying horizontal velocity $v_0$ at the point ' A ', the string becomes slack when, the bob reaches at the point ' D '. The ratio of the kinetic energy of the bob at the points $B$ and $C$ is ______ -.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \frac{1}{2} \mathrm{mv}_{\mathrm{A}}^2=\frac{1}{2} \mathrm{mv}_{\mathrm{B}}^2+\mathrm{mgh} \\ & \Rightarrow \frac{1}{2} \mathrm{~m}(5 \mathrm{~g} \ell)=\frac{1}{2} \mathrm{mv}_{\mathrm{B}}^2+\mathrm{mg} \frac{\ell}{2} \\ & \Rightarrow \frac{5 \mathrm{mg} \ell}{2}-\frac{\mathrm{mg} \ell}{2}=\mathrm{KE}_{\mathrm{B}} \\ & \Rightarrow \mathrm{KE}_{\mathrm{B}}=2 \mathrm{mg} \ell \\ & \frac{1}{2} \mathrm{mv}_{\mathrm{C}}^2=\frac{1}{2} \mathrm{mv}_{\mathrm{D}}^2+\mathrm{mg} \frac{\ell}{2} \\ & \Rightarrow \mathrm{KE}_{\mathrm{C}}=\frac{1}{2} \mathrm{mg} \ell+\mathrm{mg} \frac{\ell}{2}=\mathrm{mg} \ell \\ & \Rightarrow \frac{\mathrm{KE}_{\mathrm{B}}}{\mathrm{KE}_{\mathrm{C}}}=2\end{aligned}$

questions.q: Arrange the four graphs in descending order of total work done; where W1,W2,W3 and W4 are the work done corresponding to figure a,b,c and d respectively.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
As seen from figure, work done in first graph, Wa=0.

Now, work done in figure b, Wb=+ve, and that in figure c, Wc=+ve, >Wb.

In last graph, work done is Wd=-ve.

So, the descending order of total work done is 

⇒Wc>Wb>Wa>Wd

⇒W3>W2>W1>W4

questions.q: A body is moving unidirectionally under the influence of a constant power source. Its displacement in time $\mathrm{t}$ is proportional to :
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & P=\operatorname{constant} \Rightarrow \mathrm{FV}=\text { constant } \\ & \Rightarrow \mathrm{m} \frac{\mathrm{dV}}{\mathrm{dt}} \mathrm{V}=\text { constant } \\ & \int_0^{\mathrm{V}} \mathrm{VdV}=(\mathrm{C}) \int_0^{\mathrm{t}} \mathrm{dt} \\ & \left(\frac{\mathrm{V}^2}{2}\right)=\mathrm{Ct} \\ & \mathrm{V} \propto \mathrm{t}^{1 / 2} \\ & \frac{\mathrm{ds}}{\mathrm{dt}} \propto \mathrm{t}^{1 / 2} \\ & \int_0^{\mathrm{S}} \mathrm{ds}=\mathrm{K} \int_0^{\mathrm{t}} \mathrm{t}^{1 / 2} \mathrm{dt} \\ & \mathrm{S}=\mathrm{K} \times \frac{2}{3} \mathrm{t}^{3 / 2} \\ & \mathrm{~S} \propto \mathrm{t}^{3 / 2}\end{aligned}\therefore$ displacement is proportional to $(\mathrm{t})^{3 / 2}$

questions.q:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion $\mathbf{A}$ and the other is labelled as Reason $\mathbf{R}$
Assertion A: In a central force field, the work done is independent of the path chosen.
Reason R: Every force encountered in mechanics does not have an associated potential energy.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below
options: Both $\mathbf{A}$ and $\mathbf{R}$ are true but $\mathbf{R}$ is NOT the correct explanation of $\mathbf{A}$
Both $\mathbf{A}$ and $\mathbf{R}$ are true and $\mathbf{R}$ is the correct explanation of $\mathbf{A}$
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Assertion is correct as central forces are conservative in nature, i.e. work done is independent of path.

Reason is true as some forces in mechanics like, friction are non-conservative because work done depends on path and only conservative forces have an associated potential energy.
Also, reason does not explain assertion.

questions.q: A body of mass <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>m</mi></math> dropped from a height <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>h</mi></math> reaches the ground with a speed of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>0</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>8</mn><msqrt><mi>g</mi><mi>h</mi></msqrt><mo>.</mo></math> The value of work done by the air-friction is:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
K1+U1=K2+U2+Wf
Wf: work done against friction
0+mgh=12mv2+0+Wf
mgh=12m0.64gh+Wf
Wf=0.68mgh
Work done by friction Wf'=-Wf=-0.68mgh

questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
4000×V+mg×V=P
60×7464000+20000=V
V=1.9 m s-1

questions.q: A body of mass $50 \mathrm{~kg}$ is lifted to a height of $20 \mathrm{~m}$ from the ground in the two different ways as shown in the figures. The ratio of work done against the gravity in both the respective cases, will be :
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution: Work done by gravity is independent of path. It depends only on vertical displacement so work done in both cases will be same.

questions.q: A block of mass 25 kg is pulled along a horizontal surface at a constant velocity by a force at an angle $45^{\circ}$ with the horizontal. The friction coefficient between the block and the surface is 0.25. The work done by the pulling force for a displacement of 5 m of the block is:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Block travels with uniform velocity
So $\quad \mathrm{a}=0 \Rightarrow \mathrm{~F} \cos 45^{\circ}=$ friction
$\begin{aligned}
& \frac{\mathrm{F}}{\sqrt{2}}=\mu\left[\mathrm{mg}-\frac{\mathrm{F}}{\sqrt{2}}\right] \\ & \frac{\mathrm{F}}{\sqrt{2}}=0.25\left[25 \times 9.8-\frac{\mathrm{F}}{\sqrt{2}}\right] \\ & \Rightarrow \quad 1.25 \frac{\mathrm{~F}}{\sqrt{2}}=61.25 \\ & \mathrm{~F}=\frac{61.25 \times \sqrt{2}}{1.25}=49 \sqrt{2} \\ & \mathrm{~W}_{\mathrm{ext}}=\mathrm{FS} \cos 45^{\circ} \\ &=49 \sqrt{2} \times 5 \times \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}=245 \mathrm{~J}
\end{aligned}$

questions.q: A block of mass <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>10</mn><mo> </mo><mi>kg</mi></math> is moving along <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>x</mi></math>-axis under the action of force <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>F</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>5</mn><mi>x</mi><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">N</mi></math>. The work done by the force in moving the block from <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></math> to <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>4</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></math> will be _______ <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">J</mi></math>.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Work done is W=∫Fdx

It is given that

F=5x N

So, work done is 

W=∫245xdx=5x2224⇒W=5(16-4)2=30 J

questions.q: A block moving horizontally on a smooth surface with a speed of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>40</mn><msup><mrow><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi></mrow><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math> splits into two equal parts. If one of the parts moves at <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>60</mn><msup><mrow><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi></mrow><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math> in the same direction, then the fractional change in the kinetic energy will be <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>x</mi><mo>:</mo><mo> </mo><mn>4</mn></math> where <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo></math> ________.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
2m×40=60×m+mv
V=20 m/s
Now ΔKE=KEf-KEi=12 m×(20)2+12 m×(60)2-122 m×(40)2
ΔKE=12 m(800)⇒KEi=122 m×(40)2=12 m×3200
Fractional change =ΔKEKEi=14

questions.q: A circular table is rotating with an angular velocity of $\omega \mathrm{rad} / \mathrm{s}$ about its axis (see figure). There is a smooth groove along a radial direction on the table. A steel ball is gently placed at a distance of $1 \mathrm{~m}$ on the groove. All the surfaces are smooth. If the radius of the table is $3 \mathrm{~m}$, the radial velocity of the ball w.r.t. the table at the time ball leaves the table is $x \sqrt{2} \omega \mathrm{m} / \mathrm{s}$, where the value of $x$ is _____.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & a_c=\omega^2 x \\ & \frac{v d v}{d x}=\omega^2 x \\ & \int_0^v v d v=\int_1^3 \omega^2 x d x \\ & \frac{v^2}{2}=\omega^2\left[\frac{x^2}{2}\right] \\ & \frac{v^2}{2}=\frac{\omega^2}{2}\left[3^2-1^2\right] \\ & v=2 \sqrt{2} \omega \\ & x=2\end{aligned}$

questions.q: To maintain a speed of 80 km h-1 by a bus of mass 500 kg on a plane rough road for 4 km distance, the work done by the engine of the bus will be _____ kJ. [The coefficient of friction between tyre of bus and road is 0.04]
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
It is given,

v=80 km h-1

m=500 kg

S=4 km

μ=0.04

The power due to friction is 

Pf=Fv where F=μmg

=0.04500×9.8×80×518 W

Hence, the work done by the engine in overcoming the friction is

W=Pft=Pfdv

⇒W=20×9.8×80×518×4×10380×518=784 kJ

questions.q: A pendulum is suspended by a string of length 250 cm. The mass of the bob of the pendulum is 200 g. The bob is pulled aside until the string is at 60° with vertical as shown in the figure. After releasing the bob, the maximum velocity attained by the bob will be _____ m s-1. (if g=10 m s-2)
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Velocity will be maximum at the bottom point when potential energy of the pendulum will be zero(considering bottom point as reference for potential energy).

12mv2=mgl-lcos60°v=gl=10×2.5=5 m s-1
